links.outcome: SEPERA performance and net benefit versus existing nomograms and logistic regression on same data
links.effect: SEPERA best across validation cohorts (pooled AUROC 0.77, AUPRC 0.61); higher net benefit than other models; correctly predicted ssEPE in 72 (68%) of 106 benign-biopsy cases vs 47 (44%) logistic regression, 0 Sayyid, 13 (12%) Soeterik non-MRI, 5 (5%) Soeterik MRI.
links.quote: SEPERA was well calibrated and had the best performance across all validation cohorts (pooled AUROC of 0·77 [95% CI 0·75-0·78] and pooled AUPRC of 0·61 [0·58-0·63]).

links.outcome: AUROC differences across demographic and clinical subgroups in algorithmic audit
links.effect: No evidence of model bias; no significant difference in AUROC when stratified by race, biopsy year, age, biopsy type, biopsy location, and D'Amico risk group.
links.quote: In the algorithmic audit, no evidence of model bias was observed, with no significant difference in AUROC when stratified by race, biopsy year, age, biopsy type (systematic only vs systematic and MRI-targeted biopsy), biopsy location (academic vs community), and D'Amico risk group.

links.outcome: Generalisation from community-hospital training data to external academic centres in three sites
links.effect: Trained on 1022 cases from a community hospital network and externally validated on 3914 cases at three academic centres, SEPERA was well calibrated with pooled AUROC 0.77 across validation cohorts.
links.quote: SEPERA was well calibrated and had the best performance across all validation cohorts (pooled AUROC of 0·77 [95% CI 0·75-0·78] and pooled AUPRC of 0·61 [0·58-0·63]).
